# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: SW-APT-01 (EyePACS, then APTOS 2019, Simulated)
- Period: week 11 (starting 2026-03-16)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift detected that retinal scans from this clinic no longer match the characteristics of the scans used to validate the AI model (drift score 1.00, where 0.5 indicates similarity to training data and 1 indicates clear divergence).

Consequently, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified from the 50 scans evaluated this week, as expert grades for these images have not yet been received. The AI model is referring a higher proportion of patients than usual: 90% of this week's scans, compared with 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of potentially missed cases has not been estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Significant reduction in image resolution, sharpness, and overall image quality, consistent with a camera change, faulty capture settings, or downsampling (category: camera or image quality; confidence 85%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- Drift score is 1.00, indicating scan characteristics diverge entirely from the training baseline.
- Mean image resolution decreased by 78.1% from 1020.0 px in training to 224.0 px in the flagged week.
- Mean sharpness dropped by 81.1% from 0.000399 to 7.53e-05.
- Mean quality score dropped by 77.3% from 0.5 to 0.113.
- Mean contrast decreased by 32.0% from 0.0963 to 0.0655, and mean brightness decreased by 15.5% from 0.373 to 0.315.
- Referral rate increased by 31.5% from 0.685 to 0.9, with referral score mean rising from 0.193 to 0.392 (+103.2%) across 50 scans.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI deployment at this clinic because scan characteristics drifted beyond validated parameters, preventing verification of the catch rate. It is recommended to direct this clinic's scans to human grading until the following checks are complete:

Checks:
- [ ] Verify the camera hardware and export settings to determine why image resolution fell to 224 pixels.
- [ ] Check for recent software updates, compression configurations, or pipeline transformations resizing incoming images.
- [ ] Inspect camera optics for focus calibration and lens cleanliness.
- [ ] Review clinical intake logs to determine if high-severity pathology is also overrepresented alongside image degradation.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
